 J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 16.12.2016 at about 6.15 a.m. the petitioner was riding a motor cycle bearing No.
KA-51-EC-6582 from his friend house at Sarjapura road, Haralur cross towards Haralur village to attend RSS class slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road,
when he reached near O Zone apartment, at that time the driver of the HGV Tanker bearing No.KA-51-9179 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Sakra hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy,
aged about 15 years, studying in 8th standard.
On account of the injuries she is permanently disabled and she lost happiness, physically and mentally.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the HGV lorry.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed its respective written statement.
5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent in its written statement averred that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that accident has not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Tanker.
Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-51-B-9179 and its validity.
Further contended that the petitioner has filed complaint more than 8 days after the said accident with an intention to fasten the said liability against the respondent insurance company.

Further contended that Master Keerthi Sagar N vs Smt.Bhagyamma on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161347267/
2 neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions u/s 134 and S.158 (6) of the MV Act.

Further denied the age avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the claim petition with cost.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the HGV/Tanker bearing registration No.KA-51- B-9179 on 16.2.2016 at about 6.15 a.m. near O Zone Apartment, Haralur Main Road, Haraluru,
Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

P19 and one witness is examined as PW4 and got marked the document at Ex.P20.
8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent has examined Senior Medical Record Keeper is examined as RW1 and got marked the document at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
9. Heard the arguments.

R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:-
During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 to PW4.
Further he argued that, the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and Master Keerthi Sagar N vs Smt.Bhagyamma on 2 April, 2019

Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued by denying the manner of the accident as alleged in the petition and contended that accident has not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the tanker, on the other hand, the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-EC-6582 as there were three minor children were proceeding on a motor cycle without wearing helmet.

Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2.
13.
On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
14. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

To substantiate the said contention he has produced prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P6 such as FIR, Complaint,
mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet respectively.

15. On perusal of complaint marked at Ex.P2 reveals that, complaint has been lodged by PW1 i.e.,
the father of the petitioner on 24.12.2016.

Based on the complaint FIR marked at Ex.P1 has been registered against the driver of the tanker in Cr.No.170/2016 by HSR Layout Traffic police for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC and S. 134(A&B) of IMV Act.
Ex.P2 is the mahazar drawn by the I.O. also corroborates the Ex.P1.
IMV report at Ex.P4 reveals that the cause of accident was not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.

Ex.P5 is wound certificate reveals the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and on perusal of charge sheet at Ex.P8 reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the offending vehicle driver for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.

16. The petitioner has examined one witness as PW4, he has reiterated the similar facts as stated by the PW1.
17.
The counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that the petitioner has filed complaint after lapse of 8 days of the incident.
On perusal of Ex.P2 complaint the PW1 has stated the reasons for delay in lodging the complaint.

18. Further argued that the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the said accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle along with two pillion riders without wearing helmet.
So, the rider of the motor cycle i.e., the petitioner has also contributed for cause of accident.
19. The respondent No.2 has examined Senior Medical Record Keeper of Sakra Hospital as RW1.
He has produced the documents marked at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2, such as authorization letter and true copy of MLC register.
He has stated in his evidence that in Ex.R2 not mentioned the number of the vehicle.
20. On the other hand the counsel for the petitioner has argued that motor cyclist may be minor and may not be having a licence cannot be held to be negligent or contributory negligent.

sentences.text: 24. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved her case that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tanker bearing registration No.KA-51-B-9179.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
25. ISSUE NO.2:- PW1 being the father of the petitioner has stated in his evidence that petitioner has met with an accident on 16.12.2016 at about 6.15 a.m. and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to Sakra hospital, Kachohalli, Bengaluru, wherein he took the treatment as inpatient.

The doctor is of the opinion that the injury Nos. 1 to 3 are grievous in nature and injury Nos. 4 &
5 are simple in nature.
PW1 has produced Ex.P8 discharge summary, which reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 16.12.2016 and discharged on 20.1.2017.
The petitioner underwent tracheostomy for prolonged intubation.
He has gradually weaned off ventilation and started on and NG feeds.
Currently he is right hemiparesis present, he has been advised for physiotherapy and speech therapy.
Again he was admitted on 15.2.2017 for bone flap replacement and underwent cranioplasty with autologous bone flap done and discharged on 20.2.2017.
27. PW2 being the Medical Record Technician at Sakra Hospital, Bengaluru has produced the documents marked at Ex.P14 to Ex.P17 such as authorization letter, case sheet, CT scan and X- rays.

28. PW3 being the neurosurgeon at BGS Hospital, has stated in his evidence that petitioner was admitted with history of RTA and was operated at Sakra hospital for traumatic brain injury with left fronto-tempero parietal acute SDH-/right frontal SDH/EDH left cerebellar region.
He underwent left FTP decompressive craniectomy on emergency basis.
He was tracheostomised and eventually decannulated.

29. The petitioner was evaluated on 28.12.2017 at BGS hospital, and found to have history of right sided weakness upper limb>>lower limbs speech disturbances, generalized weakness, vertigo,
memory disturbances and gain disturbances and decreased sleep.
On examination he had motor dysphasiaright, hemi paresis and again taxia.
He has produced Ex.P18 and Ex.P19 such as OPD prescriptions and assessment report.

Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and PW2 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
30. The case of the petitioner is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 15 years.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered a lot.
PW1 has produced Ex.P8 discharge summary, which reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 16.12.2016 and discharged on 20.1.2017.
Again he was admitted on 15.2.2017 and discharged on 20.2.2017.
PW1 has also produced school certificate of the petitioner, marked at Ex.P7, which shows that the petitioner was studying in VIII standard and after the accident he ha snot attended the school.
During the said period either father or mother, one has to look after their son by leaving their work.
So, I deem it fit to grant Rs.50,000/- under the head of inconvenience caused to the parents during the treatment period.
Therefore, Rs.50,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
31. The contention of PW1 is that, they have spent Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
She has produced the medical bills at Ex.P9 to the extent of Rs.9,33,102/- supported with prescriptions and advance receipts marked at E.P11.
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.9,33,102/- under the head of medical expenses.

32. Further contention of the PW1 is that, prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy,
aged about 15 years, student.

Due to the accidental injuries, he has became permanent disability throughout his life and unable to attend his classes and it affected on his educational career and also Master Keerthi Sagar N vs Smt.Bhagyamma on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161347267/
6 on his bright future.

sentences.text: Now also he has not recovered from the injuries sustained in the accident, he is getting head ache and giddiness often and often he lost total sensation over right hand.
His memory power is considerably reduced.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW1, he has admitted that at the time of accident his son was aged about 14 years.

33. PW3 being the Neuro surgeon has stated in his evidence that he has examined the petitioner on 15.3.2018 and noted the following problems;
a)He has difficulty to speak/eat, work with right hand, walk on elevations, feels imbalance and always has sense of falling without support b) He has difficulty in making day-to-day decision, reasoning and judgment c) He has reduced day time alertness and require supervision of day time activities d) He will require assistance while walking 34.

As per neuropsychological assessment of cognitive ability by Dr. Pratibha Sharan which revealed significant deficits in verbal mental speed, verbal fluency, category fluency, verbal learning and memory logical memory with bilateral frontal lobe, bilateral temporal lobe involvement.
According to DGHS telescopic sum formula his cognitive and neurobehavioural disability amounts to 48.66% .

35. Based on the said PW3 has assessed the whole body disability as 47% according to the guidelines published in text book of neurosurgery Wilkins and Rengachary second edition volume I.
36.

Therefore, Rs.3,00,000/- is granted under the head of disability.
38. PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accident petitioner took the treatment as inpatient and also as outpatient.
On perusal of Ex.P8 discharge summary, which reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 16.12.2016 and discharged on 20.1.2017.
Again he was admitted on 15.2.2017 and discharged on 20.2.2017.
So, one must attend her during the above said period.
Further as per the findings of the PW3 being the neurosurgeon the petitioner has difficulty to speak/eat, work with Master Keerthi Sagar N vs Smt.Bhagyamma on 2 April, 2019

Needs help for almost all the activities of daily living."
39.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW3, he has stated that now hemiparesis is 3+/5, it is gradually improving, but chances of complete recovery is less.
So, considering the above facts, the petitioner needs attendant throughout his life.

Therefore, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- under the head of amenities, attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.,
40.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
Sl.No. Compensation heads Amount 1. Pain and suffering Rs. 1,50,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 50,000-00  and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs. 9,33,102-00 4.
Permanent disability Rs. 3,00,000-00 5. Loss of amenities, Attendant, Rs. 1,50,000-00
Nourishment and conveyance  charges  Total Rs.15,83,102-00 41.
LIABILITY:

As I have already discussed in issue No.1 that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tanker bearing No.KA-51-B-9179.
42.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of bus bearing No. KA-51-B-9179 and its validity.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.
43. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV Act as against the respondents is partly allowed with cost.

O R D E R The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV Act as against the respondents is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,83,102/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
